name: Big-data promotional saturation
description: The brief period in which big data became a ubiquitous promise in boardrooms, marketing conferences, and service pitches.
cause_of_death: 2013 misuse backlash, 2014 disillusionment, and retirement from the 2015 emerging-technologies hype chart; technical use continued.

sources.title: Big data: 4 predictions for 2014
sources.note: Calls 2013 the awareness breakthrough and records widespread backlash; also documents late-2013 big-data-as-a-service rhetoric.

sources.title: Gartner 2015 Hype Cycle: Big Data is Out, Machine Learning is in
sources.note: Reports disappearance from the 2015 emerging-technologies chart after 2014 disillusionment; retirement does not imply technical abandonment.

sources.title: Big Data is an over-used buzzword, and this Twitter bot proves it
sources.note: Contemporary evidence of indiscriminate marketing use and explicit ridicule.

entries.gloss: A saturated promotional label for extracting transformative value from large and varied data.

examples.text: Could you bring the printouts so we can unlock the big data in this meeting?
big data became everyone's most hated buzzword in 2013

entries.rationale: The Guardian identifies 2013 as the breakthrough year for awareness and widespread misuse. The 2015 chart retirement and contemporary parody support the declining promotional phase. The onset is an estimated uptake boundary and 2017 an estimated fade; big data remains a valid technical field.

entries.gloss: A promotional promise of outsourced big-data capability as an accessible service.

examples.text: Let us provision these printouts as big data-as-a-service for the review.
Big data-as-a-service will become a big deal

entries.rationale: The Guardian says the idea began to creep into the latter parts of 2013 and forecasts expansion in 2014. The peak and fade are estimated within the broader big-data promotional cluster; the service concept continues and this does not establish an independent annual frequency series.
